source.title: Topology and geometry of data manifold in deep learning

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices and references.
record.tranche_reason: Measures topological descriptors in trained CNNs and tests their association with test accuracy/generalization across models and training settings, a different measure from the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports topology and PHdim correlations with test accuracy, plus topology changes during training and under adversarial attacks. It does not test random-label memorization, width beyond interpolation, CNN versus fully connected performance, optimizer comparisons, batch-size effects, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. Figure 6's individual model values are figure-only; no exact values are stated in text.
record.test_reason: The study measures representation topology and its association with CNN test performance. It does not test any specified version. In particular, its topological descriptors are not V7's magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation sharpness. Varying training hyperparameters across models does not establish the optimizer, batch-size, or dropout comparisons required by V4–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase captures the authors' conclusion that CNN training simplifies representation topology and that last-layer topology can predict generalization. However, the reported inverse correlation with test accuracy error has internally inconsistent outcome wording; it should not be converted into an unqualified directional claim about error.
record.recipe_differences: Uses persistent-homology and topology measurements in trained CNN representations rather than the interventions or measurements specified in the claim versions. Training used Adam; reported generalization-related comparisons vary several hyperparameters.
record.method_sensitivity: Architecture, activation function, dataset, training epoch, and training hyperparameters (regularization, learning rate, weight decay, batch size, augmentation) are varied or discussed as affecting the observed topology/generalization relationship.

fits_no_version.finding: Across training epochs, last-layer E10 correlates negatively with test accuracy: r = -0.92 for ResNet and -0.965 for SE-ResNet.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Last-layer representation topology tracks test accuracy during training in these CNNs.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 50 CIFAR-10 ResNets trained to 100% training accuracy, Section 4.2 reports a topology–performance correlation of r = -0.9. Its description of the outcome as error conflicts with the accuracy caption and stated interpretation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Last-layer topology is associated with held-out performance across trained ResNets; the direction relative to error requires clarification.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report better test accuracy with Swish in their ResNet-101 activation comparison, without numerical accuracy values.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation choice affects test performance and representation topology in the tested CNN.

record.problems: The principal cross-model relationship is reported as a correlation and does not establish causation. Individual Figure 6 model values are not given in text. The paper says the 50 models vary several hyperparameters, limiting attribution to any one condition. The text calls the correlation statistically significant but gives no p-value or uncertainty interval.
record.rows_left_out: No required rows omitted. Figure-only individual points and clusters in Figure 6 are retained as an aggregate figure-only row because the text does not describe individual values.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization, including chance-level random-label test performance.
Test-error changes when width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity or convolutional initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under specified tuning conditions and recovery recipes.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce the penalty.
Dropout effects on held-out error, small-data failure, underfitting, and interaction with augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Accuracy effects of removing highly memorized training examples versus equal-sized random removals.

record.verdict_notes: With 100% training accuracy, cross-model test error also represents the generalization gap, but the predictor remains topology rather than V7's sharpness. Appendix B adds PHdim–accuracy relationships and a higher-homology correlation of r = -0.87; neither tests a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Large versus small batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.
